title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: GitLab.com
providers.scope_notes: Group IP controls require Premium/Ultimate. Do not transfer Self-Managed 400-day/configuration options to GitLab.com.

controls.name: Restrict access by IP address
controls.what: Limits UI and API access to the group to listed CIDRs, including group/project tokens, deploy keys and CI clone operations.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: IP restrictions apply to project and group access tokens, service accounts, deploy keys, and deploy tokens.

controls.name: Enforce SSO-only authentication for Git and Dependency Proxy activity
controls.what: Git over HTTPS/SSH and Git-related API calls by users need an active SSO session; not enforced for bot tokens or CI jobs.
controls.quote: For Git activity over SSH and HTTPS, users must have at least one active session signed-in through SSO before they can push to or pull from a GitLab repository.

no_control.what: Group SSO enforcement does not apply to API requests (PAT or OAuth).
no_control.quote: SSO enforcement does not apply to API requests. However, you can disable password and passkey authentication for enterprise users to prevent password-based API access.

controls_unknown: Whether a GitLab.com group owner can block or allowlist third-party OAuth applications that members authorize (no group-level control found).
Whether a GitLab.com group owner can set a shorter maximum token lifetime than the 365-day default (docs describe this only for administrators/Self-Managed).

authentication.summary: Personal/project/group access tokens, OAuth bearer, CI_JOB_TOKEN and deployment credentials for limited endpoints.

federation.details: CI OIDC ID tokens federate outward to external services. CI_JOB_TOKEN is a native short-lived credential, not generic external federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: Group restriction covers UI/API/Git, including service-account and project/group tokens. Runner coordination and other documented exceptions remain.

lifetime.summary: 2 hours on GitLab.com (configurable only by Self-Managed/Dedicated admins)

renewal.summary: Refresh exchange invalidates the previous access/refresh pair.

administration.summary: Scopes and project/group membership, token rotation/revocation, SAML enforcement and CI job-token allowlists.
administration.conditions: Group IP controls require Premium/Ultimate. Do not transfer Self-Managed 400-day/configuration options to GitLab.com.

sso.details: API requests are not SSO-checked, except Git-related endpoints when the Git/Dependency Proxy SSO option is on.

sso.ui: Group > Settings > SAML SSO > Enforce SSO-only authentication for Git and Dependency Proxy activity for this group (Git-related API only)

expiry.api: POST /oauth/token response expires_in (7200); GET /oauth/token/info shows expires_in

reads.ui: Project > Secure > Audit events; filter by user and date, look for repository_download_operation

token_format.notes: Access token prefix not documented. Application secret uses gloas-. Default expires_in 7200 s.

log_sources.name: GitLab audit events (group/project/instance)
log_sources.notes: Retained indefinitely. Group/project events need Premium/Ultimate; API date range max 30 days per query. Streaming needs Ultimate.

log_sources.name: api_json.log / production_json.log
log_sources.notes: Self-Managed only. Per-request remote_ip, ua, user_id, username, route/path; correlation_id in production_json.log.

log_sources.name: /oauth/token/info
log_sources.notes: Returns resource_owner_id, scope, expires_in, application.uid, created_at for a live token

log_sources.name: User profile > Access > Applications (Authorized applications)
log_sources.notes: Per-user list of authorized OAuth apps with Revoke

credential_id_fields.notes: OAuth client ID that owns the token

lifecycle_events.notes: Subset of requests with audited scope
Sign-in with OAuth (OmniAuth), not API token use

anomaly_cues: user_authorized_oauth_application for an app created minutes earlier (consent phishing)
oauth_application_updated changing redirect URI followed by new authorizations
many users authorizing the same non-trusted app in a short window
API activity for a user from IPs never seen in their interactive sessions
refresh-token use from a host different from the app's normal egress

containment.steps: User revokes the app under Access > Applications > Authorized applications; app owner calls POST /oauth/revoke with client_id, client_secret, token; delete the application to remove all grants and tokens; Renew secret to stop the app from obtaining new tokens.
containment.notes: Deleting the app removes all tokens. Effect of revoking a refresh token on outstanding access tokens is not documented; access tokens expire after 2 hours.

sample_query.query: GET /oauth/token/info with header Authorization: Bearer <suspect token>
sample_query.purpose: Identify the app (application.uid), user (resource_owner_id) and scope of a found token

unknown: audit event for OAuth token revocation
whether revoking refresh token kills access tokens

calls.reveals: resource_owner_id, scope, expires_in, application for the OAuth token
calls.log_notes: Doorkeeper introspection; no documented audit event

calls.reveals: projects the OAuth user is a member of

calls.log_notes: Premium/Ultimate to save to DB; Ultimate to stream; public projects use public_repository_download_operation (not saved)

unknown: Whether archive downloads over Git (git clone via OAuth) emit the same repository_download_operation event
